checks: Writing z=r+2j gives output base (p+r)/2+j. Distinct residues give distinct image cosets and every half-lattice base has the integer inverse 2q−p.
The continuous Jacobian is 2^{-d}, the centered linear margin scales by one half, and the affine pushforward gives each class centroid. This includes closed pure-base boundary fibers.

The centroid coefficients are proportional to c_rM_r, and each simplex coefficient vector is achievable by dividing by M_r. For a relative-interior point, extend the segment from the average of all listed centroids slightly beyond the point in the hull, giving a representation with every coefficient positive. The argument includes repeated centroids and a singleton hull.
The relabeling subtracts (a·s)/2 from the margin. The binary convex hull has the stated exact endpoint sections, and (1/2)B_d at the relabeled base zero strictly exceeds εB_d.
The frozen statement retains the positive-mass convention and two-fiber example from source §3.

overlap.comparison: This predecessor separately reparametrizes parity decimations of an all-discrete polygon. It does not identify the common-anchor half-lattice measure or its centroid criteria.
The one-integer-coordinate ray chart represents original cap and moment laws, with no shifted-lattice cosets, pooling, or relabeling witness.

readability: An occupied class in the centroid statements is a positive-mass class, as specified by M_r>0.
